clue.text: Shameless, having had a close shave

definitions.meaning: read literally: with the cheeks and chin shaved bare of whiskers

explanation.walkthrough: 'close shave' suggests a narrow escape, but here it is a literal razor job.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazen lie is told openly and without embarrassment; the second reading takes the compound word at face value as a naked chin.

clue.text: Dame Clara's targets

definitions.meaning: Dame Clara Butt was a famous English contralto, so this is her name with a possessive
archery targets, or the mounds behind them, on a range

explanation.walkthrough: Dame Clara Butt (1872-1936) was a celebrated British concert singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's surname with apostrophe-s, and archery targets, the mounds on a shooting range, share the same spelling.

clue.text: Dreadfully alarmed to find broken rocks in the way

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a terrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to find shattered stones blocking the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadfully' signals the anagram of ALARMED TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed stone used to make or repair a road surface is the material laid in the way.

clue.text: One constructing castle in Spain -infanta's is transformed to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess is changed in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'castle in Spain' is an old idiom for a daydream, like a castle in the air; an infanta is a Spanish princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who builds castles in Spain is a daydreamer, given to grand imaginings.

clue.text: Unlikely to crumple, like a stonewaller?

definitions.meaning: describing fabric treated so that it does not wrinkle
a stonewaller in cricket is a batsman who defends doggedly and refuses to leave the crease, his batting position

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line the batsman stands at; a stonewaller blocks every ball rather than scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated fabric that resists wrinkling; read whimsically, a batsman who stubbornly holds his position at the crease.

clue.text: Horse, for example, offered for sale that's hard to shift

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, an example of a drug
on the market means up for sale

explanation.surface: A horse being sold proves very hard to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' suggests an animal at auction, but it is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names goods nobody wants to buy, so a merchant cannot move them.

clue.text: Messenger — one of those on horseback, possibly

definitions.meaning: the Greek root of the word means a bearer of tidings, as with Gabriel

definitions.text: one of those on horseback, possibly
definitions.meaning: '... on horseback' is a savoury of oysters wrapped in bacon, so one oyster could be called this

explanation.walkthrough: Angels on horseback is a British savoury: oysters wrapped in bacon and grilled, served on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly beings in scripture carry God's tidings to people, and each oyster in the bacon savoury takes the same name.

clue.text: Old coin collection is a valuable possession

parts.note: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A set of ancient coins is worth a good deal to its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The as was a Roman coin, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something owned that has worth, on a balance sheet or in life, counts as a resource.

clue.text: Greedily devour Cheddar, for example

definitions.meaning: to stuff oneself with food, eating gluttonously
Cheddar ... in Somerset is a famous limestone ravine

explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar looks like the cheese, which suits 'devour', but it is the Somerset ravine that gave the cheese its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To gobble food voraciously; and Cheddar Gorge in south-west England is a deep, narrow canyon.

clue.text: It helps those who want to make the cut at St Andrew's

definitions.text: It helps those who want to make the cut at St Andrew's

parts.words: It helps those who want to make the cut at St Andrew's
parts.note: 'make the cut' suggests golfers qualifying for the later rounds at the famous course, but the cutting is of grass

explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf; making the cut means qualifying for the final rounds of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that trims grass helps keepers keep the greens and fairways short.

clue.text: Coach repeated direction for beginner

parts.note: to coach is to train someone

indicators.note: repeated says the compass point that follows comes twice in a row

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A coach keeps giving the same instruction to a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' tempts a solver toward an instruction from the coach, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still learning a job under instruction is a novice in it.

clue.text: A foreign second team appears to slacken off

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a crew is a team, of rowers for instance

explanation.surface: An overseas reserve side looks to be easing up in its effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A foreign' asks for 'a' in another language: French UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a threaded fastening by turning it is to make it slack.

clue.text: Charitable donations one collected back in Indian town

indicators.note: back says the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction
the gifts have collected one, taking it in among their letters

parts.note: alms are gifts to the poor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Gifts to charity gathered and brought home to a town in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' puts I inside ALMS to make ALMIS; 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: This hill station in the Himalayan foothills was the British Raj's summer capital, now spelt Shimla.

clue.text: Concerned about immediate future, as result of premature birth?

definitions.meaning: dealing only with the near time ahead, not the long run
a baby born early has had a brief pregnancy, a gestation cut short

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a pregnancy whose term was not full.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies aimed at quick results look only to the near future; a baby born early came after a brief gestation period.

clue.text: An altogether sound direction

parts.note: a 'sound direction' is an instruction in a musical score, and this one tells everyone to play together

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'reliable', but it means musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian marking in a score tells the whole orchestra or choir to play or sing at once.

clue.text: Silk hat worn by clumsy actor is an encumbrance aloft

indicators.note: a hat worn by someone surrounds his head, so the hat goes round the actor

parts.note: a topper is a top hat, traditionally made of silk
a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: An inept performer's tall hat gets in his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat 'worn by' the actor encloses him; top-hamper is a ship's upper rigging and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical term is the upper rigging and gear of a ship, a weight high up that hampers it.

clue.text: Vicious brawl in Hyde Park

parts.note: rotten means nasty or vicious
a row is a noisy quarrel or brawl

explanation.surface: A nasty fight breaks out in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the sandy riding track along the south side of Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous bridleway is located in the royal park in London, so the clue defines it by where it lies.

clue.text: Fortitude shown by French in Alpine river

parts.note: en is the French word for 'in'
the Durance flows from the French Alps to join the Rhône

explanation.surface: Courage displayed by French people out on a mountain river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the people, but 'French in' asks for 'in' in French, EN.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to bear hardship steadily over time is courage of a patient kind.

clue.text: Buttress supporting church needs check at the top

indicators.note: at the top says the word for check comes first, in a down answer

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
for means in favour of, supporting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church's flying buttress needs inspecting at its summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttress' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'check' is REIN, not an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up or strengthen something, as a wall is shored up, is to support it.

clue.text: Superficial courtesy fashionable in old epistles

indicators.note: read as 'able to be fashioned', so the letters can be shaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Polite letters of the past displayed a merely surface courtesy that was in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' is the anagram signal: O (old) plus EPISTLES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means formal politeness, often with a hint that it is only for show.

clue.text: One relying, perhaps, on spin doctor? That's right

parts.note: i.e., id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A public figure leans on a spin doctor, and is told that is quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctor' looks like one phrase, but 'spin' ends the definition and 'doctor' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin dryer is a machine that removes water from laundry by whirling it, so it relies on spinning.

clue.text: Relief of pain Galen contrived in East

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged physician's name inside the word for the East

parts.note: Asia is the East, the Orient

indicators.note: contrived means devised or worked out, so the name's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The ancient physician Galen devised a painkiller in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' turns GALEN into NALGE, which goes 'in' ASIA. Galen was a famous ancient Greek doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term means inability to feel pain, the state an anaesthetic or painkiller brings about.

clue.text: Silly action against Conservative

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: A foolish move by opponents of the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: C for Conservative refers to Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful or ludicrous caper is a foolish piece of behaviour.

clue.text: Frozen like some eels, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: jellied eels are a traditional London dish

explanation.surface: Eels set in jelly are said to be ice-cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels, eels set in their own jelly, are a classic East London food.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Latin for frost, means icy cold.

clue.text: During epidemic left Winchester, say

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left comes during the word for widespread, inside it

parts.note: rife, like epidemic, means widespread

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned the city of Winchester while a plague was raging.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is an English cathedral city, but here it is the American rifle maker. 'During' puts L inside RIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester repeating firearm is a famous example of a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: Wound up, but stopped

definitions.meaning: concluded or brought to a close

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' could mean agitated or a wound clock; here it means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean brought to a finish or concluded.

clue.text: Joint is covered with this fat. finally, in Spanish dish

indicators.note: in puts the picked letter inside the name of the rice dish

parts.note: paella is the Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A cut of meat is coated in fat and then added to a paella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a roast; it is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is a small bone that sits over the front of the knee and shields it.

clue.text: Benevolent cardinal, possibly, in the flesh

parts.note: kind means benevolent
red is the cardinal's colour, the scarlet of his robes, so a cardinal might be described by it

explanation.surface: A kindly churchman of high rank appears in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the flesh' usually means 'in person'; here it means related by blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives share blood and body, the 'flesh and blood' of a family, so they are akin by nature.

clue.text: Way in which champion competed

indicators.note: in which says the road abbreviation holds the next word inside it

parts.note: RD, road, is a way
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: The route on which a champion contested the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' signals that the champion sits inside the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To have run a race against others is to have taken part in a contest.

clue.text: Documentary evidence of championship feat

parts.note: a title is a championship, as in a boxing title
a deed is a feat or exploit

explanation.surface: Papers that prove someone won a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Documentary' here means in document form, not a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal paper proving ownership of property is written evidence of a right.
